<p>We are excited to introduce Grok 4.1, which brings significant improvements to the real-world usability of Grok. Our 4.1 model is exceptionally capable in creative, emotional, and collaborative interactions. It is more perceptive to nuanced intent, compelling to speak with, and coherent in personality, while fully retaining the razor-sharp intelligence and reliability of its predecessors. To achieve this, we used the same large scale reinforcement learning infrastructure that powered Grok 4 and applied it to optimize the style, personality, helpfulness, and alignment of the model. In order to optimize these non-verifiable reward signals, we developed new methods that let us use frontier agentic reasoning models as reward models to autonomously evaluate and iterate on responses at scale.</p>
<h2 id="silent-rollout-november-114-2025"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#silent-rollout-november-114-2025">Silent Rollout, November 1–14, 2025</a></h2>
<p>We conducted a gradual silent rollout of preliminary Grok 4.1 builds to a progressively larger share of production traffic across grok.com, X, and mobile apps. During the two-week silent rollout we ran continuous blind pairwise evaluations on live traffic.</p>
<div class="not-prose bg-card relative my-12 flex items-center justify-center p-6 sm:p-12"><div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-6 sm:flex-row sm:items-center"><div class="mt-6 text-center sm:mt-0 sm:text-left"><h1 class="text-primary text-3xl tracking-tighter">Grok 4.1</h1><p class="text-secondary text-2xl">vs. previous Grok</p></div><div class="flex grow items-center justify-center"><div class="relative size-64"><div class="recharts-responsive-container" style="width:100%;height:100%;min-width:0"></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Compared to the previous production model in traffic, Grok 4.1 is preferred 64.78% of the time.</p>
<h2 id="state-of-the-art-general-capability"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#state-of-the-art-general-capability">State-of-the-Art General Capability</a></h2>
<p>Grok 4.1 establishes a new standard in blind human preference evaluations.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-12 lg:-mx-32 lg:my-20"><div class="border-border divide-border relative flex min-w-0 shrink-0 flex-col divide-y border"><div class="bg-card flex items-start justify-between px-6 py-4"><div class="w-full leading-6"><h3 class="text-sm font-medium">LMArena Text Leaderboard</h3></div></div><div class="flex grow flex-col divide-y"><div class="flex grow overflow-hidden"><div class="relative flex grow overflow-x-auto sm:overflow-x-hidden"><div class="recharts-responsive-container w-full !min-w-[550px] sm:!min-w-0" style="width:100%;height:600px;min-width:0"></div></div></div><div class="hidden h-12 justify-between divide-x sm:flex"><div class="flex h-full items-center px-4 text-sm" style="width:310px"><span class="text-sm font-medium">Overall Style Control Elo</span></div><div class="flex h-full grow items-center justify-between gap-2 px-4"><span class="text-secondary text-sm font-medium">1325</span><span class="text-secondary text-sm font-medium">1525</span></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>In LMArena&#x27;s <a href="https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard/text">Text Arena</a>, Grok 4.1 Thinking (code name: <code>quasarflux</code>) holds the #1 overall position with 1483 Elo —a commanding margin of 31 points over the highest non-xAI model. Grok 4.1 in its non-reasoning mode (code name: <code>tensor</code>) uses no thinking tokens for an immediate response and ranks #2 at 1465 Elo. Grok 4.1 non-thinking surpasses every other model’s full-reasoning configuration on the public leaderboard. Grok 4.1 significantly surpasses Grok 4, which had an overall rank of #33.</p>
<h3 id="emotional-intelligence"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#emotional-intelligence">Emotional Intelligence</a></h3>
<p>To measure progress on our model’s personality and interpersonal ability, we evaluated Grok 4.1 on <a href="https://eqbench.com/">EQ-Bench3</a>. EQ-Bench is a LLM-judged test, evaluating active emotional intelligence abilities, understanding, insight, empathy, and interpersonal skills. The test set contains 45 challenging roleplay scenarios, most of which constitute pre-written prompts spanning 3 turns. The benchmark evaluates the performance of the models by validating the models’ responses against several criteria. Additionally, the benchmark conducts pairwise comparisons to report a normalized Elo computation for each model in the leaderboard.</p>
<p>We report the rubric score and normalized Elo score by running the <a href="https://github.com/EQ-bench/eqbench3">official benchmark repository</a>. The scores were computed with the default sampling parameters, prescribed judge (Claude Sonnet 3.7), and no system prompt in accordance with the benchmark.</p>

<h3 id="creative-writing"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#creative-writing">Creative Writing</a></h3>
<p>We also measured the performance of 4.1 models on the <a href="https://eqbench.com/creative_writing.html">Creative Writing v3 benchmark</a>. In this benchmark, models generate responses to 32 distinct writing prompts across 3 iterations. Similar to EQ-Bench, scores are computed using both rubrics and model battle normalized Elo.</p>

<h3 id="reduced-hallucinations"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#reduced-hallucinations">Reduced Hallucinations</a></h3>
<p>Fast (non-reasoning) models equipped with search tools deliver quick answers, but they can be vulnerable to factual errors due to constrained reasoning depth and limited tool-call budgets.</p>
<p>In Grok 4.1 post-training, we focus on reducing factual hallucinations for information-seeking prompts. Subsequently we have observed significant reductions in hallucination rate for sampled production info-seeking prompts.</p>
<p>We evaluate hallucination rate on a stratified sample of real-world information-seeking queries from production traffic. We also evaluate FActScore, which is a public benchmark consisting of 500 biography questions on individuals.</p>

[&amp;_summary]:text-xl prose-sm text-primary max-w-none leading-6"><p>San Francisco offers a mix of iconic landmarks, natural beauty, and vibrant neighborhoods. Here are some of the best places to visit, based on their popularity, cultural significance, and unique appeal:</p><ul><li><p><strong>Golden Gate Bridge</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: An engineering marvel and SF’s most iconic landmark, offering stunning views, especially at sunrise or sunset.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Walk or bike across the 1.7-mile span, visit the Welcome Center, or view it from Battery Spencer or Fort Point for epic photos.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Dress for wind and fog. Free to walk, but biking rentals cost ~$10-$15/hour.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Alcatraz Island</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: A former federal prison turned National Park, rich in history with stories of infamous inmates like Al Capone.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Take a ferry for a guided audio tour of the cellhouse, explore the gardens, or join a night tour for a spookier vibe.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Book tickets 2-3 weeks ahead via Alcatraz Cruises ($40-$50). Ferries depart from Pier 33.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Fisherman’s Wharf &amp; Pier 39</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: A lively waterfront with sea lions, street performers, and classic SF clam chowder in sourdough bread bowls.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Watch sea lions at Pier 39, visit the Aquarium of the Bay, or grab seafood at places like Fog Harbor Fish House.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Crowded, so go early. Parking is pricey (~$10-$20/hour); consider public transit.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Chinatown</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: One of North America’s oldest and largest Chinatowns, packed with culture, food, and history.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Stroll Grant Avenue, visit the Chinatown Gate, explore markets, or eat dim sum at Good Luck Dim Sum or City View.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Try bubble tea or fortune cookies from Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory. Cash is handy for small shops.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Golden Gate Park</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: A massive urban park (bigger than Central Park) with museums, gardens, and quirky attractions.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Visit the de Young Museum, California Academy of Sciences, or Japanese Tea Garden. Rent a boat at Stow Lake or spot bison in the paddock.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Free to enter, but museums charge ($15-$25). Bike rentals available (~$25/day).</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Mission District</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: A vibrant, artsy neighborhood known for colorful murals, taquerias, and hip vibes.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Check out street art on Clarion Alley, eat burritos at La Taqueria or El Farolito, or sip coffee at Ritual Coffee Roasters.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Visit Dolores Park for people-watching and city views. Evening walks can feel lively but safe in groups.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Lands End &amp; Sutro Baths</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: Rugged coastal trails with Pacific Ocean views and ruins of historic baths.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Hike the Lands End Trail, visit the Cliff House, or explore the Sutro Baths ruins. Don’t miss the nearby Legion of Honor museum.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Free parking, but arrive early. Trails are moderate; wear sturdy shoes.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Coit Tower &amp; North Beach</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: Coit Tower offers 360-degree city views, and North Beach is SF’s “Little Italy” with great food and history.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Ride the elevator to Coit Tower’s top ($10), wander Telegraph Hill, or dine at Tony’s Pizza Napoletana.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Steep stairs to the tower; consider a rideshare. Visit City Lights Bookstore for literary vibes.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Painted Ladies &amp; Alamo Square</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: Iconic Victorian houses featured in “Full House” with a postcard-worthy skyline backdrop.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Snap photos from Alamo Square Park, picnic, or explore nearby Haight-Ashbury for hippie history.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Best lighting in late afternoon. Free, but respect private homes.</li></ul></li><li><p><strong>Twin Peaks</strong> </p><ul><li><strong>Why Visit</strong>: A hilltop with panoramic views of SF, perfect for day or night visits.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>What to Do</strong>: Drive or hike up for vistas of the bay, bridge, and skyline. Bring binoculars for stargazing.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Tips</strong>: Chilly at night; bring layers. Accessible by car or Muni bus.</li></ul></li></ul><p><strong>Additional Tips</strong>:<!-- --> </p><ul><li><strong>Weather</strong>: SF’s microclimates vary. Layers are key; fog (aka “Karl”) can roll in fast.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Transport</strong>: Use Muni ($2.50/ride), BART, or rideshares. Parking is tough and expensive.<!-- --> </li><li><strong>Timing</strong>: Spring (Mar-May) or fall (Sep-Nov) offer milder weather. Summer can be foggy.</li></ul><p>If you’re prioritizing, Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz, and Golden Gate Park are musts for first-timers. For specific interests (e.g., food, art, history), let me know, and I can tailor suggestions! Want me to check X for real-time visitor feedback or generate a map of these spots?</p></div></div></div></div><div class="divide-y"><div class="flex items-start justify-between px-6 py-4"><div class="w-full leading-6"><h3 class="!m-0 text-lg">Grok 4.1</h3></div><div class="text-primary bg-card rounded-full border px-3 py-1 text-sm">New</div></div><div class="h-[300px] overflow-hidden sm:h-[400px]"><div class="minimal-scrollbar h-full overflow-y-auto px-6 py-3"><div class="prose text-primary max-w-none text-pretty prose-hr:border-border prose-p:text-primary/85 prose-li:text-primary/85 prose-a:text-primary prose-a:no-underline prose-a:border-b prose-a:border-primary/20 hover:prose-a:border-primary/50 prose-a:transition-colors [&amp;_.heading-anchor]:border-b-0 prose-headings:text-primary prose-headings:font-display prose-headings:font-medium prose-headings:tracking-tight prose-headings:mt-12 prose-h3:mt-10 prose-h4:mt-6 prose-h5:mt-6 prose-h6:mt-6 prose-h1:text-4xl prose-h2:text-2xl prose-strong:font-semibold prose-strong:text-primary prose-th:py-2 prose-th:font-medium prose-th:text-primary prose-td:font-normal prose-td:text-primary/85 prose-td:py-2 prose-code:before:content-none prose-code:after:content-none prose-code:rounded prose-code:bg-primary/[0.03] prose-code:shadow-[0_0_0_1px_hsl(var(--primary)/0.08),0_1px_2px_hsl(var(--primary)/0.06)] prose-code:px-1 prose-code:py-px prose-code:text-[0.9em] prose-code:leading-normal prose-code:text-primary/75 prose-code:font-mono prose-code:font-normal dark:prose-code:bg-white/[0.05] dark:prose-code:shadow-[0_0_0_1px_hsl(0_0%_100%/0.1),0_1px_3px_hsl(0_0%_0%/0.2)] prose-a:pb-px [&amp;_summary]:py-2 [&amp;_summary]:text-xl prose-sm text-primary max-w-none leading-6"><p>San Francisco (SF) is packed with iconic sights, vibrant neighborhoods, and stunning views — perfect for first-timers or repeat visitors. Here are some of the best places to visit, blending must-sees with a few lesser-known gems. I&#x27;ve focused on timeless favorites that remain top recommendations in 2025.</p><ul><li><strong>Golden Gate Bridge</strong><br/>The ultimate SF symbol. Walk or bike across for epic views (it&#x27;s free for pedestrians), or hit spots like Battery East or Crissy Field for photos.
